title: Switch
overview: Binary on/off that applies immediately, without a separate submit.
apply_when: A setting that should persist as soon as they flip it.
not_when: A form checkbox that waits for submit, or a sticky pressed button (`aria-pressed`) that should stay a button.

vs.why: a press that commits, including toggle-button / aria-pressed

role.apply_when: A setting that should persist as state without a form submit.
role.not_when: A form flag that waits for submit (checkbox).

size.overview: Highest in the size hierarchy — the easiest to hit.
size.apply_when: The view's main instance, or full-width on a small viewport.
size.not_when: A dense toolbar or a third option next to the main control.

size.apply_when: Ordinary use in forms, pages, and chrome.
size.not_when: The only control on a mobile screen that should span the width.

size.overview: Lowest in the size hierarchy — densest.
size.apply_when: Inline or chrome that sits beside content.
size.not_when: The page's primary instance, or a control under 44×44.

composition.overview: The setting name sits with the switch.
composition.not_when: A switch with no visible name.

state.overview: Off or on as stored, available.

state.apply_when: A mouse or trackpad can reach it.
state.not_when: Hover is the only on/off cue.

state.overview: Keyboard or AT is on the switch. Must stay visible.
The setting cannot change. Must stay perceivable.
state.not_when: A required setting dropped from the tab order.

state.overview: The setting is on and already applying.
state.not_when: A visual slide with no accessible state.
Off that looks identical to disabled.

accessibility.overview: The switch names the setting, not On/Off alone.
accessibility.not_when: The only name is a color.

accessibility.overview: On/off is exposed as checked state (or switch role).
accessibility.not_when: A checkbox faked as a switch with no role.

accessibility.overview: The hit area includes the label.

keyboard.overview: Enter toggles when that is the house.
